newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank/Portugal rate cut seen last before autumn.
newsitem.headline: Bank/Portugal rate cut seen last before autumn.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal's official 30-basis point rate cut on Friday will be the last before the autumn but not the last for the rest of the year, analysts said.
The Bank of Portugal's repurchase, or repo, rate dropped to 5.7 percent.
Anaylsts expected the repo rate to fall to just above five percent by year end, providing no problems arise with the escudo or inflation.

"We will have more cuts in the last quarter of the year. I think that the repo is going (to) fall a further 50 or 70 basis points (by year end)," said Jorge Ferraz of IMF-Informacao de Mercados Financeiros.
"I would not say five percent, but it will be close," echoed Isabel Cabral of Fincor.

The cuts, which also lowered the absorption rate, or the rate at which the central bank drains funds from the market, to 5.4 percent surprised many analysts. The central bank was widely expected to wait a while longer before easing rates.
The early rate cuts reflect confidence that the June inflation figures, due from the National Statistics Institute (INE) on Monday, would re-establish the downward trend, analysts said.
Month-on-month May inflation jumped to 0.7 percent from April's 0.2 percent, taking the year-on-year change to 2.1 percent after 1.8 percent the month before.
Analysts predict year-on-year June inflation between 2.0 and 2.4 percent.

The central bank's cut in both the drain and repo rates significantly and by the same amount, which keeps the gap between them from widening, suggested there would probably be no further easing in the short-term, most analysts said.
Joao Lourenco of brokers Siemca said the current strength of the economy would also keep rates steady in the near-term.
Many economists predict the Portuguese economy will grow by at least 3.5 percent in 1997, above the government's 3.0-percent forecast in its budget programme.

"Taking account of the significant economic growth, there could still be some adjustment to come. But right now, based on current conditions, the room for further falls seems to be almost exhausted," he said.
But one analyst with a foreign bank said "the repo rate could already be around 5.5 percent and therefore, I still expect there to be a further 20 basis point cut in the short-term."
Short-term money rates reacted immediately to the central bank's move, with the tommorrow/next rate dropping to 5.65/68 percent from 5.95/97 percent at the open.
